loot: Lithara can provide (if she trusts the party): a partial map of the Marrow Halls and Heart Chamber (grants advantage on navigation checks), the Bone Warden's standby phrase in Celestial, 2 potions of mind shielding (grants immunity to psychic damage for 1 hour, brewed from divine parasite secretions), and a dreamcatcher talisman she crafted from divine bone fragments (when worn, grants advantage on Wisdom saves against dream effects within the corpse, does not require attunement)

scenes.name: The Wound Gate Descent
scenes.description: The party descends through the Wound Gate — the breach in Auldrath's ribcage — fighting or evading Threshold Leeches and the Bone Warden to reach the thoracic cavity. This is the scenario's first major dungeon sequence, combining vertical traversal, parasite encounters, and the critical decision of how to handle the Bone Warden.
scenes.readAloud: The Wound Gate gapes before you like the entrance to a hell designed by a poet. Two hundred feet tall and sixty feet wide, the breach in the dead god's ribcage has calcified into a vertical maw of jagged divine bone, its edges crystallized into formations that look exactly like teeth — or perhaps they ARE teeth, grown by the corpse's immune response in a failed attempt to seal a wound that killed a deity. Beyond the threshold, the wound channel descends into amber darkness. The walls are alive — not with memory but with actual life, a thick coating of bioluminescent organisms that cling to the exposed divine tissue like coral to a reef. They pulse with their own rhythm, out of sync with the Heartbeat, creating a disorienting double-pulse of light that makes the passage seem to breathe. The smell hits you next: ozone and ancient stone and that faintly sweet corruption, stronger here where the divine flesh is raw and exposed. And beneath it all, reverberating up through the wound channel like thunder through a canyon, the Heartbeat. Closer now. Louder. You can feel it in your teeth. Something moves in the amber darkness below — something large, rhythmic, patient. The sound of bone grinding on bone echoes up the passage. The Bone Warden is on its patrol.

skillChecks.success: The character descends the wound channel safely using rope and climbing gear, maintaining control on the slippery parasitic coating.
skillChecks.failure: The character slips on the bioluminescent coating and slides 30 feet before catching themselves. They take 1d6 bludgeoning damage and their movement disturbs a cluster of Threshold Leeches.

skillChecks.success: The party navigates past the Bone Warden by hiding in side cavities as it passes. They avoid combat entirely and conserve resources for deeper in the corpse.
skillChecks.failure: The Bone Warden detects the party and advances, filling the wound channel with its grinding bulk. The party must fight, flee, or attempt to communicate with it.

skillChecks.success: The Bone Warden accepts the party's claim that they are here to restore boundaries. It steps aside and allows passage. On a critical success (25+), it provides a limited escort through the thoracic cavity.
skillChecks.failure: The Bone Warden does not understand or does not believe the party's claim. It attacks. (It can be re-engaged in conversation if combat is halted — it does not hold grudges, only follows its programming.)

skillChecks.success: The character identifies the Threshold Leeches before they attack and knows that bright light (Daylight spell or equivalent) drives them into hiding for 1 hour. This allows the party to pass through leech-infested sections safely.
skillChecks.failure: The character does not identify the leeches in time. The first awareness of their presence is when one drops from the ceiling and attaches to the character carrying the most magical items.

skillChecks.success: The character takes in the first sight of the thoracic cavity — a space the size of a small country, lit by crystallized divine veins, with calcified organs rising like mountains — without losing their composure.
skillChecks.failure: The character is stunned for 1 round by the sheer cosmic scale of what they are seeing. The thoracic cavity is so vast that the far wall is lost in amber haze, and the realization that they are inside a body triggers a moment of existential vertigo.

enemies: 6 Threshold Leeches (stirge stats, CR 1/2, HP 2, AC 14, energy drain: 1d4 force damage per round, suppresses 1 random magic item while attached, DC 13 to detach)
1 Alpha Threshold Leech (stirge stats, HP 10, AC 14, energy drain: 1d6 force damage per round, suppresses 1 random magic item, DC 15 to detach)
combatEncounters.tactics: The leeches drop from the ceiling in a coordinated wave, targeting characters with the most active magic items or strongest Threadwalker resonance. The Alpha hangs back and drops onto the most vulnerable character after the initial swarm has engaged. They retreat into wall crevices when half their number are killed. Bright light (Daylight or equivalent) drives all leeches into hiding immediately.
combatEncounters.terrain: The wound channel is 60 ft wide, 200 ft tall, and descends at a 45-degree angle. The walls are coated in slippery bioluminescent growth (DC 14 to maintain grip while climbing). The leeches use the walls and ceiling for ambush positions. The narrow width of the channel makes area-of-effect spells effective but risks damaging the parasitic ecosystem (cosmetic but Lithara will be upset).

enemies: 1 Bone Warden (shield guardian stats, CR 7, HP 142, AC 17, immune to psychic and radiant damage, resistant to nonmagical physical damage, can cast Compelled Duel at will, DC 15)
combatEncounters.tactics: The Bone Warden advances methodically, filling most of the channel's width. It uses Compelled Duel on the strongest-looking melee fighter and then focuses attacks on that target. It does not pursue beyond the wound channel. It fights until destroyed, then collapses into bone fragments that reassemble in 1d4 hours. It can be communicated with during combat — talking is a free action, and if a character makes a successful DC 16 Persuasion check in the right language mid-fight, the Warden immediately stops attacking.
combatEncounters.terrain: The wound channel narrows slightly where the Bone Warden patrols (40 ft wide here). The parasitic bioluminescence flares with each impact, creating brief flashes of bright light. Side cavities (DC 14 Perception to spot) provide hiding spots but are small (fits 1 Medium creature). The descent angle means gravity works against melee fighters trying to close distance uphill.

scenes.roleplayNotes: The descent through the Wound Gate is the scenario's first dungeon crawl and should establish the rhythm of exploration mixed with environmental hazard and combat. The Bone Warden encounter is the key decision point: fighting it is possible but costly (it reassembles, so it is a recurring threat), sneaking past requires excellent Stealth, and negotiating requires knowing the right language and saying the right things. Lithara's standby phrase makes this trivial, but only if she trusts the party enough to share it. If the party neither fights nor negotiates and simply avoids the Warden, it continues its patrol and may be encountered again at inopportune moments. The first sight of the thoracic cavity should be narrated as a moment of genuine awe — this is not a dungeon, it is the inside of a god, and the scale should be overwhelming.
loot: From the hidden side passage (DC 17 Investigation): the remains of a previous Astral Warden expedition — 3 desiccated corpses in Warden robes; a partial map of the thoracic cavity and Marrow Halls (grants advantage on navigation checks); an Amulet of Proof Against Detection and Location (requires attunement); a journal describing the expedition's failure (plot information about the Dream and the previous attempt to survey the corpse); 45 gp in mixed Astral coinage

acts.title: Act 2: The Dreaming Deep
acts.description: The party navigates the Marrow Halls and the Heart Chamber, encountering the corpse's internal ecosystem, the crystallized memories of a dead god, and the increasingly coherent Dreaming Voice. This act is the scenario's longest and most varied, combining exploration, puzzle-solving, combat, and roleplay in roughly equal measure. The party must find a route from the thoracic cavity to the skull, gathering information and resources along the way. The two major environments — the Marrow Halls (a maze of divine bone filled with memories) and the Heart Chamber (a vast interior space dominated by the still-beating Heart) — offer contrasting challenges: the Halls are claustrophobic and psychologically intense, while the Chamber is open and filled with dangerous creatures. The act culminates in the party choosing their final approach to the Skull Sanctum: the fast but dangerous Aorta route or the slower but safer Marrow Hall route.
objectives: Navigate the Marrow Halls and reach the Heart Chamber
Interact with the crystallized memories to learn about the fragment and the corpse's layout
Survive or negotiate the Marrow Halls' hazards (Memory Golems, variable gravity, dream manifestations)
Reach the Heart Chamber and encounter the Dreaming Voice's second manifestation
Discover the Heart's role in amplifying the Confluence fragment
Choose a route to the Skull Sanctum (Aorta or Marrow Hall continuation)
Optional: defeat the Cerebral Devourer in the Heart Chamber
Optional: find the hidden divine marrow chamber for a vision and resources

scenes.name: The Memory Maze
scenes.description: The party enters the Marrow Halls — the labyrinthine tunnel network through Auldrath's divine bones — and encounters the crystallized memories that line the walls. Navigation is the primary challenge, complicated by variable gravity and the disorienting effect of the memories themselves. The Dreaming Voice makes its first appearance, a confused and fragmented divine subconscious trying to understand who is inside it.
scenes.readAloud: The tunnel ahead is not made of stone. It is made of bone — divine bone, dense and warm to the touch, with a grain like wood and a hardness like adamantine. The walls are not smooth but textured with branching channels where something once flowed, and in those channels, frozen in amber crystal, are the memories of a god. The first one catches you off guard. You brush the wall with your shoulder and the world SHIFTS — suddenly you are standing in a void of absolute white, and before you is a line. Not a line drawn on a surface but a line in reality itself, a boundary between HERE and THERE, and you are reaching out with hands that are not your hands — hands that span light-years — to draw another line, and another, dividing the white void into compartments that will one day be called planes. The vision lasts three seconds. Then you are back in the tunnel, breathing hard, your shoulder tingling where it touched the wall. The amber crystal in the channel beside you glows a little brighter, as if pleased to have been noticed. Ahead, the tunnel branches. And branches. And branches again. The Marrow Halls stretch in every direction, a three-dimensional maze of divine bone, and somewhere in the branching, gravity decides it has better things to do than pull downward. Your feet leave the floor. Your stomach lurches. And a voice — not heard but FELT, vibrating in your bones like the subsonic hum of a cathedral organ — says: 'You are... in me? I am... what am I?'

skillChecks.success: The character navigates the Marrow Halls competently, keeping the party on a route toward the Heart Chamber. Reduced to DC 12 with the Astral Wardens' partial map or automatic with Lithara's guidance.
skillChecks.failure: The party becomes lost. Add 1d4 hours of wandering, during which they encounter one additional random memory vein (roll on the memory table) and one additional hazard (variable gravity shift or parasite encounter).

skillChecks.success: The character maintains awareness that the memory vein's vision is not real. They experience it as an observer — vivid and moving but clearly separate from their own identity.
skillChecks.failure: The character is absorbed into the memory for 1d4 rounds, incapacitated, experiencing it as if they were Auldrath. They feel the god's emotions, think the god's thoughts, and when they return to themselves, they are shaken but carry a fragment of divine perspective.

skillChecks.success: The character adapts smoothly to a gravity transition, maintaining footing and orientation as 'down' shifts 90 degrees.
skillChecks.failure: The character tumbles uncontrollably through the gravity shift, taking 1d6 bludgeoning damage and ending up in a different tunnel branch. DC 14 Survival to find their way back, or the party follows the sound of their voice.

skillChecks.success: The character responds to the Dreaming Voice with compassion and clarity, framing their presence in terms the divine subconscious can understand. The Voice provides a fragment of navigational intuition: advantage on Survival checks in the Marrow Halls for 8 hours.
skillChecks.failure: The Voice does not understand the character's response. It cycles through confusion and agitation before dissolving back into scattered memories. No benefit, but no harm.

skillChecks.success: The character successfully queries a memory resonance zone for specific information — the layout of the Heart Chamber, the nature of the fragment's connection to the neural crystal, or a detail of Auldrath's history relevant to the current situation.
skillChecks.failure: The query triggers a cascade of overlapping memories that overwhelms the character — 2d4 psychic damage and the character is dazed (disadvantage on Intelligence checks) for 1 hour.

enemies: 1 Memory Golem (stone golem stats, CR 10, HP 178, AC 17, immune to psychic damage, vulnerable to thunder damage, slam attacks deal additional 2d6 psychic damage)
combatEncounters.tactics: The Memory Golem is looping a fragment of the Dawn War — it swings its fists in patterns that correspond to an ancient battle, and it only attacks creatures that enter its chamber or disrupt its loop. It can be bypassed entirely if the party finds an alternate route (DC 14 Survival). It can be calmed with a DC 18 Arcana check (redirecting its loop) or a DC 16 Performance check (harmonizing with its emotional tone). In combat, it uses its Slow ability first, then focuses on the nearest target. It does not pursue beyond its chamber.
combatEncounters.terrain: A roughly spherical chamber 40 ft in diameter carved from divine bone. The walls are covered in active memory veins that create overlapping visions of the Dawn War — these provide half cover to any creature adjacent to a wall (the visual distortion makes targeting difficult) but also risk triggering memory absorption (DC 12 Wisdom save if you press against a wall for cover). The Memory Golem's thunderous attacks cause the chamber to vibrate, potentially triggering multiple memory veins simultaneously (DC 13 Wisdom save for all creatures in the chamber when this happens).

enemies: 4 Marrow Stalkers (phase spider stats, CR 3, HP 32, AC 13, radiant damage instead of poison, phase through divine bone instead of Ethereal Jaunt)
combatEncounters.tactics: The Marrow Stalkers ambush at a gravity transition zone where the party is disoriented. Two emerge from each wall simultaneously. They target isolated characters, use hit-and-run tactics (emerge, attack, phase back into bone), and retreat into the bone if any single stalker takes more than 15 damage in one round. A DC 15 Nature check mid-combat reveals they fear Memory Golems — if one is activated nearby, all Stalkers flee immediately.
combatEncounters.terrain: A gravity transition zone — a junction where three tunnel branches meet and gravity pulls in three different directions. Characters must make a DC 13 Acrobatics check at the start of each turn to maintain their footing. The Marrow Stalkers are unaffected by the gravity shifts (they move through solid bone). The junction is 30 ft across with tunnels branching at odd angles.

scenes.roleplayNotes: The Marrow Halls are the scenario's most psychologically intense section. The memories should be played for emotional impact — these are not data points but lived experiences of a being that existed for eons. The memory of drawing the first boundary is serene and god-like; the memory of the Dawn War is chaotic and terrifying; the memory of watching the first mortal die is quiet and profound. The Dreaming Voice's first appearance should be eerie and sad — this is not a threatening entity but a confused one, a fragment of consciousness trying to remember what it was. Characters who respond with empathy will get more out of this scenario than characters who respond with aggression. Lithara, if present, is visibly moved by the memories and may need to be pulled away from a particularly vivid one. She knows which memory veins contain useful information and which are 'just' beautiful.
loot: From the hidden memory vein (DC 16 Investigation): experiencing Auldrath's memory of creating the first boundaries grants a permanent scar of insight — advantage on all checks to communicate with or understand the Confluence, but disadvantage on checks to destroy a Confluence fragment (the character hesitates, understanding the Confluence's pain)

From the hidden divine marrow chamber (DC 15 Acrobatics to access): immersion grants benefits of a long rest and +10 max HP for 24 hours on a successful DC 18 Constitution save; up to 3 vials of divine marrow can be bottled (each functions as a potion of superior healing, 8d4+8 HP, with a side effect of 1d4 hours of divine visions)
Memory resonance zone query (DC 15 Arcana): specific information about the corpse's layout, the fragment's defenses, or Auldrath's history — not physical loot but potentially invaluable intelligence

scenes.name: The Heart of a Dead God
scenes.description: The party reaches the Heart Chamber — the vast central cavity of the corpse dominated by Auldrath's calcified heart, which still beats. Here they encounter the corpse's most dangerous ecosystem, the Cerebral Devourer, and the Dreaming Voice's second and most significant manifestation. They must decide their approach to the Skull Sanctum.
scenes.readAloud: The tunnel opens and the world falls away. You step out of the Marrow Halls into a space so vast that your mind refuses to process it as an interior. The Heart Chamber is a mile across. The ceiling — the underside of Auldrath's ribcage — arches hundreds of feet overhead, each rib a mile-long curve of divine bone, and between them, gaps where the intercostal muscle has dissolved let silver Astral light pour in like sunlight through a cathedral's clerestory windows. The floor is covered in a thick layer of crystallized divine sediment that crunches underfoot and glows faintly amber. And in the center of it all, suspended by calcified arteries the size of bridge cables, hangs the Heart. It is the size of a fortress. Its surface is a landscape of crystallized veins and calcified muscle, and it is BEATING. Every thirty seconds, the massive organ contracts with a sound that you feel in your spine — a deep, subsonic THUD that sends a pulse of amber light racing through every crystallized vein in the chamber. For three seconds, the world is golden and warm and you can feel something that is almost love. Then the light fades, and the Heart relaxes, and the thirty-second count begins again. Between the heartbeats, things move in the sediment. Shapes circle the Heart in slow, territorial orbits — the Hearthbound, creatures that have fused themselves to the dead god's cardiovascular system and feed on each pulse of residual divinity. They are beautiful and wrong. And somewhere beneath the sediment, at the very edge of your awareness, something intelligent is watching you with an enormous, hungry eye.

skillChecks.success: The character braces against the Heartbeat's shockwave and holds their position.
skillChecks.failure: The character is pushed 10 feet away from the Heart by the shockwave. If this pushes them into difficult terrain (the sediment), they must make a DC 12 Dexterity save or fall prone.

skillChecks.success: The character resists the Heartbeat's dream-pulse and maintains awareness.
skillChecks.failure: The character experiences a 6-second flash of Auldrath's current dream — incapacitated for 1 round. The dream is of standing at a doorway, looking through, and seeing everything on the other side dissolving into a blur of color.

skillChecks.success: The character finds and can access Lithara's research station in the calcified left lung — maps, notes, specimen jars, and supplies that provide crucial information about the Heart, the Aorta, and the route to the skull.
skillChecks.failure: The character finds the station but triggers the Glyph of Warding on the entrance (5d8 thunder damage, DC 15 Dexterity save for half). Lithara, if present, is mortified.

skillChecks.success: The character matches the Heart's resonance frequency, synchronizing the party's heartbeats with Auldrath's. For 1 hour: immunity to the Heartbeat's shockwave and Wisdom saves, advantage on saves against dream effects in the Skull Sanctum, and clear perception of the Dreaming Voice without skill checks.
skillChecks.failure: The attempted resonance produces a discordant frequency that agitates the Heart — for the next 10 minutes, the Heartbeat occurs every 15 seconds instead of 30, doubling the rate of shockwaves and dream-pulses.

skillChecks.success: The character determines that the Confluence fragment is stimulating the Heart through the crystallized nervous system. The Heart is the fragment's power source. Stopping it would weaken the fragment enormously but would also kill the Dream and every organism in the corpse.
skillChecks.failure: The character senses a connection between the Heart and the fragment but cannot determine its nature. They know the Heart is important but not how.

enemies: 2 Hearthbound Drones (gargoyle stats, CR 2, HP 52, AC 15, radiant damage, death burst: 2d6 radiant in 15-ft radius on death, DC 13 Dex save for half)
1 Hearthbound Alpha (manticore stats, CR 3, HP 68, AC 14, radiant tail bolts 1d8+3, 30-ft regeneration aura: allies regen 5 HP/turn within 60 ft of Heart)
combatEncounters.tactics: The Alpha directs Drones to flank while it stays near the Heart for the regeneration aura. Kill the Alpha first to break coordination — Drones become confused and flee when the Alpha dies. More Hearthbound arrive after 10 rounds (2 Drones per round). This is a fight the party should win quickly or disengage from, not a prolonged battle of attrition.
combatEncounters.terrain: Open Heart Chamber. The crystallized sediment floor is difficult terrain. The Heartbeat's shockwave pushes creatures away from the Heart every 30 seconds. The calcified arteries (20 ft diameter) provide platforms above the sediment. The Heart itself is 200 ft above the floor, out of melee range. The Hearthbound can climb the arteries and fly short distances.

enemies: 1 Cerebral Devourer (scaled intellect devourer, CR 10, HP 130, AC 16, Int 19; Psychic Crush: 60-ft cone, 6d8 psychic damage, DC 16 Int save for half + stunned on fail, recharge 5-6; Devour Thoughts: melee +8, 3d8+4 psychic + DC 16 Int save or lose random proficiency for 1 hour; Body Thief: DC 16 Int save; Psychic Invisibility: invisible to creatures with Int below 12, DC 16 Perception to detect)
combatEncounters.tactics: The Devourer lurks in the divine sediment near the Heart, attracted by the party's concentrated thoughts. It targets the highest-Intelligence character first with Psychic Crush, then attempts Body Thief on a stunned target. It uses Psychic Invisibility to reposition between attacks. It retreats into the sediment if reduced below 40 HP, burrowing away to heal — it reappears in the Skull Sanctum at full strength (150 HP) for a second encounter. If the party can keep it above 40 HP and focus fire, they can kill it here and avoid the rematch.
combatEncounters.terrain: The sediment floor provides the Devourer with cover and concealment — it can submerge completely (DC 16 Perception to locate when submerged). The Heartbeat's shockwave does not affect the Devourer (it is anchored in the sediment). The chamber's vast size means ranged attackers have clear lines of sight but the Devourer's Psychic Invisibility makes targeting unreliable. Characters standing on calcified arteries above the sediment are safe from the Devourer's emergence attacks but exposed to its Psychic Crush cone.

scenes.roleplayNotes: The Heart Chamber is where the scenario transitions from exploration to urgency. The Dreaming Voice's second manifestation — 'My heart still beats. I can feel you inside me.' — should be played as a moment of genuine connection between the party and the dead god's subconscious. Auldrath is not a monster or a puzzle; it is a person (of sorts) trapped between life and death, confused and frightened by what is happening to it. The moral weight of the party's mission becomes clear here: extracting the fragment will save the Astral Sea but will also end the Dream, possibly forever. Lithara's advocacy for preserving the Dream should feel reasonable, not obstructive — she has a point, and the party should grapple with it. The strategic decision between the Aorta (fast/dangerous) and the Marrow Hall route (slow/safe) should feel consequential. Lithara strongly recommends the Marrow Halls and can provide an 8-hour route; the Aorta takes 2-3 hours but means fighting through Hearthbound the entire way.
loot: From the Cerebral Devourer's lair in the sediment (DC 17 Investigation, or track the Devourer's retreat): a +1 mace that deals extra 1d6 radiant damage against undead and constructs, a Cloak of Protection, 3 potions of greater healing, and a sealed journal belonging to a Convergence Herald detailing the Herald's mission to protect the fragment (critical plot information)

From Lithara's research station (if she grants access or party finds it): detailed maps of the Heart Chamber and Aorta approach, research notes on the Heartbeat acceleration (6 days until catastrophic reactivation), and 2 potions of mind shielding
Heart resonance synchronization (DC 17 Performance): not physical loot but a powerful tactical advantage for the Skull Sanctum — 1 hour of immunity to heartbeat effects and advantage on dream saves

acts.title: Act 3: The Sanctum of Dreams
acts.description: The party enters the Skull Sanctum for the scenario's climax. The Dream is at its most powerful here — reality is fluid, memories are physical, and the Confluence fragment is organizing everything into an increasingly coherent and hostile defense. The party must navigate the dream-logic environment, defeat or evade the Skull's guardians, and perform the delicate extraction of the fragment through a complex skill challenge. The scenario's conclusion depends on their choices: a clean extraction preserves Auldrath's legacy and yields maximum rewards; a messy extraction still succeeds but with consequences; and a catastrophic failure triggers a desperate escape sequence. Throughout, the Dreaming Voice serves as both ally and obstacle — it wants the fragment removed but fears the end of its Dream.
objectives: Enter the Skull Sanctum and adapt to the dream-logic environment
Navigate through or defeat the Skull's defensive manifestations
Reach the Confluence fragment at the skull's center
Defeat the Cerebral Devourer (if it retreated from the Heart Chamber)
Perform the extraction skill challenge (5 successes before 3 failures)
Secure the fragment and escape the corpse
Decide the fate of Auldrath's skull (report to Zerith-Ka, potential new Warden fortress)

scenes.name: Into the Dream
scenes.description: The party enters the Skull Sanctum and is immediately immersed in the Dream — a reality where thought becomes visible, gravity is a suggestion, and the memories of a dead god play out on every surface. The initial shock gives way to the realization that the Dream is aware of them, and it is marshaling its defenses.
scenes.readAloud: You step through the foramen magnum — the base of the skull, where the spinal column once connected — and reality ends. The space beyond is not a cave or a chamber or a room. It is a mind. The interior of Auldrath's skull stretches three miles in every direction, a perfect dome of divine bone, and every inch of it is alive with light. The memory web — the crystallized neural tissue that was once a god's brain — covers the skull's interior surface in an interconnected lattice of amber crystal, and all of it is firing. Every memory Auldrath ever formed plays simultaneously: the creation of planes, the death of stars, the first word ever spoken across a divine threshold, a quiet moment watching rain fall on a world that no longer exists. The light is overwhelming — amber and gold and colors you don't have names for, cascading across the curved walls in patterns that would be beautiful if they weren't so clearly the activity of a mind in distress. And at the center of it all, floating in the exact middle of the skull cavity, you see the fragment. It is small — fist-sized — and it is everything. A shard of crystal that shifts through every color simultaneously, pulsing with a light that is warm and cold and familiar and alien. Tendrils of prismatic energy extend from it into the memory web like roots into soil, drinking deep of the dead god's residual divinity. The air is not air. It is thick and warm and tastes like someone else's thoughts. You breathe in and catch a flash of a sunset you have never seen. You breathe out and see your own exhaled breath form into shapes — a word, a face, a fear — before dissolving. Your feet find a surface that shouldn't be a floor but your mind makes it one. Gravity is whatever you believe it is. And then the Dream notices you. The memory web flickers. The cascading patterns pause, just for an instant, and in that instant of stillness, every single memory on the skull's interior surface turns to look at you. Thousands of eyes. Millions. The eyes of a god, reflected in a million moments, all focused on the same point: you. Then the patterns resume, faster now, agitated, and from the web, shapes begin to pull free — figures made of amber light and crystallized thought, stepping out of the memories and into the space between, their empty eyes searching for the intruders in the dream.

skillChecks.success: The character adapts to the Dream medium without being overwhelmed. They can breathe the manifested-thought atmosphere without experiencing involuntary memory flashes.
skillChecks.failure: Each breath delivers a 6-second flash of Auldrath's current dream. The character is incapacitated for 1 round on entry and must repeat the save each round until they succeed.

skillChecks.success: The character establishes personal gravity in the skull's dream-logic space, anchoring their sense of 'down' and gaining normal movement. Characters synchronized with the Heartbeat make this check with advantage.
skillChecks.failure: The character floats uncontrollably for 1d4 rounds, tumbling through the Dream medium. DC 10 Wisdom check as a bonus action to stabilize each round.

skillChecks.success: The character masks their thoughts, preventing the Dream medium from revealing their intentions. They do not suffer disadvantage on Stealth checks within the skull.
skillChecks.failure: The character's intentions are visible as shapes and colors in the Dream medium — everyone nearby (including hostile manifestations) can perceive their emotional state and general plans.

skillChecks.success: The character maintains their sense of self against the fragment's anti-boundary aura, which attempts to blur the lines between individual consciousnesses. They do not merge perceptions with other characters.
skillChecks.failure: The character briefly merges perceptions with another random character in the anti-boundary radius — they share thoughts and senses for 6 seconds, experiencing disorienting double-vision and overlapping inner monologues.

enemies: 2 Dream Wraiths (wraith stats, CR 5, HP 67, AC 13, psychic damage instead of necrotic, thought drain: DC 14 Con save or Intelligence reduced by 1d4 until short rest, dissolve after 5 rounds)
1 Memory Golem (stone golem stats, CR 10, HP 178, AC 17, additional 2d6 psychic on slams, vulnerable to thunder)
combatEncounters.tactics: The Dream Wraiths move through the Dream medium as if flying, phasing through memory web strands and attacking from unexpected angles. They target characters whose thoughts are visible in the Dream medium (those who failed the Deception check). The Memory Golem forms from the wall and advances methodically. All three manifestations dissolve and reform 1 hour later unless the party has the Dreaming Voice's cooperation (which suppresses hostile manifestations for 2 hours) or is synchronized with the Heartbeat (which halves the spawn rate). The Dream wraiths dissolve naturally after 5 rounds regardless of HP.
combatEncounters.terrain: The Skull Sanctum has dream-logic gravity — characters can walk on any surface. The memory web on the walls provides half cover but risks memory absorption (DC 12 Wisdom save). The anti-boundary field within 60 ft of the fragment causes extradimensional spaces to malfunction and teleportation to fail. The Dream medium makes all creatures' thoughts and emotions visible, imposing disadvantage on Stealth unless thoughts are masked.

scenes.roleplayNotes: Entering the Skull Sanctum should feel like crossing a threshold (appropriate, given Auldrath's domain). The transition from the relatively comprehensible interior of the corpse to the full Dream experience should be disorienting and awe-inspiring. The Dream medium's properties — visible thoughts, dream-logic gravity, breathing memories — should be described vividly and consistently. Characters who have synchronized with the Heartbeat or befriended the Dreaming Voice have a significantly easier time here, rewarding players who engaged with the scenario's roleplay elements. Characters who brute-forced their way to the skull face a much harder climb.
loot: No physical loot in this scene — the rewards come from the extraction sequence in the next scene

scenes.name: The Extraction
scenes.description: The scenario's climax: the party reaches the Confluence fragment and must extract it from the neural crystal through a multi-stage skill challenge while the Dream fights to prevent them. This is simultaneously a skill challenge, a potential combat encounter (if the Cerebral Devourer is present), and a roleplay moment (the Dreaming Voice's final communication). The outcome determines the scenario's resolution and the rewards the party receives.
scenes.readAloud: You are close now. Close enough to touch it. The Confluence fragment hangs in the center of the skull, embedded in a mass of neural crystal that was once Auldrath's brain, and it is the most beautiful and terrible thing you have ever seen. It shifts through every color — not sequentially but simultaneously, as if it contains all of reality in a single point. The tendrils of prismatic light that extend from it into the memory web pulse with the Heartbeat's rhythm, and where they connect, the memories they touch are dissolving, replaced by something else: visions of a reality without borders, where everything is everything and nothing is separate. It is hypnotic. It is horrifying. It is a window into what the multiverse would become if the Confluence succeeds. The fragment is warm. You can feel it from here — a warmth that has nothing to do with temperature and everything to do with WANTING. It wants to connect. It wants to dissolve the boundary between itself and everything around it. Including you. The neural crystal that holds it is delicate — a web of divine nerve tissue, calcified but still structurally significant. Pull the fragment free carelessly and the crystal shatters, the memory web collapses, the Dream implodes, and you are standing in the center of a reality implosion the size of a city. Pull it free carefully — sever each tendril, stabilize the crystal, maintain the Dream's coherence — and you can extract it cleanly, leaving the skull's structure intact and the memories preserved. The Dreaming Voice is here. Not a distant echo but a presence, immediate and vast, filling the Dream medium with a quality of attention that is unmistakably divine. 'You are here for the splinter,' it says, and this time the voice is almost clear, almost coherent, almost alive. 'I know what it is now. It is the thing that killed me. It came back. It always comes back to the boundaries.' A pause. The amber light dims. 'Take it out. Please. It hurts. But...' Another pause, longer, weighted with something ancient and immeasurable. 'If you take it out, will I stop dreaming? I have been dreaming for so long. I am afraid of the silence.'

skillChecks.success: A tendril of the fragment's connection to the memory web is severed cleanly. The neural crystal cracks slightly but holds. One step closer to extraction.
skillChecks.failure: The severing is imprecise — a psychic shockwave erupts as the tendril snaps back, dealing 3d6 psychic damage to all within 30 ft (DC 15 Intelligence save for half). The Dream shudders. One failure closer to catastrophe.

skillChecks.success: The neural crystal is stabilized around the latest severance point. The Dream steadies. The character's hands move with surgical precision guided by instincts they didn't know they had.
skillChecks.failure: The stabilization attempt fails — a crack propagates through the neural crystal, and the Dream jolts violently. All creatures within the skull must make a DC 13 Wisdom save or be stunned for 1 round.

skillChecks.success: The character invokes Auldrath's domain of boundaries, creating a divine buffer between the fragment and the neural crystal. The fragment's anti-boundary aura is suppressed in a 10-ft radius for 1 minute, making the next skill check easier (DC reduced by 2).
skillChecks.failure: The invocation resonates with the fragment rather than against it — the anti-boundary aura expands to 90 ft for 1 round, causing all extradimensional spaces to dump their contents and all characters to make DC 14 Charisma saves against perception merging.

skillChecks.success: The character physically manipulates the fragment's connection to the neural crystal with exquisite precision, loosening its grip without disturbing the surrounding tissue. One more tendril free.
skillChecks.failure: The character's fingers slip — the fragment pulses defensively, dealing 2d8 radiant damage to the character (no save) and sending a shock through the memory web that spawns 1 Dream Wraith.

skillChecks.success: The character maintains the heartbeat synchronization, keeping the Dream stable and the fragment's pulses predictable. The rhythm holds. The Dream breathes.
skillChecks.failure: The synchronization breaks — the Dream's rhythm becomes erratic, and the fragment's pulses become unpredictable. All subsequent skill checks in this extraction attempt are made at disadvantage until someone re-establishes synchronization (DC 17 Performance).

enemies: 1 Cerebral Devourer — second encounter (HP 150, AC 16, Int 19; Psychic Crush: recharge 5-6, 60-ft cone 6d8 psychic, DC 16 Int save; Dream Anchor: bonus action, immune to forced movement + AC 18; Devour Thoughts: melee +8, 3d8+4 psychic + DC 16 Int proficiency suppression; Psychic Invisibility: invisible to Int below 12, DC 16 Perception)
combatEncounters.tactics: The Devourer fights in the space around the fragment, using the anti-boundary aura to its advantage. It Dream Anchors itself within 30 ft of the fragment where the anti-boundary effect is strongest. It targets characters performing the extraction skill challenge, using Psychic Crush to stun them and interrupt the process (a stunned character's skill check automatically fails). If reduced to 0 HP here, it is dead permanently. The Devourer is present only if it fled the Heart Chamber — if it was killed there, replace with a Convergence Echo encounter (mirror copies of the party).
combatEncounters.terrain: The skull's center, within the fragment's 60-ft anti-boundary aura. Teleportation fails. Extradimensional spaces malfunction. Thoughts are visible. Gravity is dream-logic. The fragment itself cannot be damaged (it is a piece of pre-creation reality and is indestructible by normal means). The neural crystal is fragile — any attack that misses a target within 10 ft of the fragment and hits the crystal instead counts as a failure on the extraction skill challenge.

scenes.roleplayNotes: The extraction is the emotional climax of the scenario. The skill challenge should be narrated with the weight it deserves — each success is a tendon of cosmic significance being severed, each failure sends tremors through the dream of a dead god. The Dreaming Voice is present throughout, commenting on the process with a mixture of hope and grief. If befriended, it actively helps — manifesting as divine hands that steady the crystal (advantage on Medicine and Sleight of Hand checks). If antagonized, it opposes — spawning manifestations and imposing disadvantage on Religion checks. The Voice's final words after a successful extraction should be played as a death scene — the Dream is ending, and Auldrath is saying goodbye to the only existence it has known for eons. The fragment, once extracted, immediately begins whispering to whoever holds it, and the party should feel the weight of carrying a piece of the intelligence that wants to reunify all of reality. The scenario's final question — 'Will you hold the boundaries?' — is not rhetorical. A character who says yes receives a divine boon but also a burden. Let the player make this choice without pressure.
loot: The Confluence Fragment — a fist-sized prismatic crystal that pulses with warmth and whispers at the edge of perception; it is a key item for the campaign's overarching plot; it radiates anti-boundary energy in a 5-ft radius when not contained (extradimensional spaces malfunction, teleportation unreliable); it can be contained in a lead-lined box or by wrapping it in Auldrath's neural crystal (Lithara can provide instructions, DC 14 Arcana to fashion a containment vessel from skull materials)

Divine Boon: Threshold Warden (awarded to a character who answers 'yes' to the Dreaming Voice's final question) — once per long rest, cast Banishment without expending a spell slot; advantage on saves against effects that transport you to another plane against your will; permanent awareness of planar boundaries within 1 mile (disadvantage on hearing-based Perception within 100 ft of convergence zones or planar portals)

Perfect Extraction Bonus (5 successes, 0 failures): Auldrath's final memory — the locations of all remaining Confluence fragments are permanently marked on the silver compass, eliminating navigation checks to find them for the rest of the campaign

Neural crystal fragments (harvested from the skull after extraction, DC 13 Arcana): 2d4 fragments worth 250 gp each to planar scholars, or they can be crafted into a Circlet of Divine Memory (requires 3 fragments + DC 16 Arcana + 8 hours of work): once per long rest, cast Legend Lore without material components

Lithara's Gratitude (if the Dream is preserved or Lithara is treated with respect): she pledges her expertise to the party's cause, becoming an available NPC ally for future scenarios; she provides a comprehensive research dossier on Confluence fragments worth advantage on Arcana checks related to the Confluence
